## Vocabulary

## Definitions

- [statement] HFT Architecture warns that exchange clocks are not synchronized. A SOL lead measured from exchange timestamps therefore needs clock-offset checks before it is interpreted as an available trading window. (low confidence) — https://hftarchitecture.com/insights/crypto-exchange-lead-lag · keywords: SOL cross-venue lead-lag after executable latency

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] HFT Architecture reports that KuCoin ranked ahead of Binance in SOL perpetual price leadership on both exchange and Tokyo receipt clocks in its July 2026 sample. The author limits the leadership conclusion to 10–700 ms. This is one vendor study, not independently replicated SOL execution evidence. (low confidence) — https://hftarchitecture.com/insights/crypto-exchange-lead-lag · keywords: SOL cross-venue lead-lag after executable latency

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Glassnode states that its public-endpoint latency measurements do not predict end-to-end order execution time. Such measurements cannot, by themselves, specify the fill delay for a SOL cross-venue strategy. (low confidence) — https://latency.glassnode.com/cex/about · keywords: SOL cross-venue lead-lag after executable latency

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Methodological inference: test a candidate SOL venue signal against executable prices after measured decision-to-fill delay and trading costs, rather than crediting the full observed lead as available profit. HFT Architecture separates prediction from execution latency, spread and fees; Glassnode separates endpoint timing from execution timing. (medium confidence) — https://hftarchitecture.com/insights/crypto-exchange-lead-lag · keywords: SOL cross-venue lead-lag after executable latency · also: https://latency.glassnode.com/cex/about

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Arrakis reports that its SOL-inclusive universe showed Binance leading Hyperliquid in trade-tape price discovery during the study window ending 26 February 2026. This is a historical venue-lead result, not a demonstrated executable SOL return. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-04) — https://arrakis.finance/blog/crypto-price-discovery · keywords: SOL cross-venue lead-lag after executable latency
- [statement] Delta Tech Systems reports a case where the order path consumed the apparent advantage of receiving a reference feed earlier. Its feed ranking alone therefore does not demonstrate an executable cross-venue signal. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-20) — https://www.delta-tech-systems.com/research/cross-venue-latency · keywords: SOL cross-venue lead-lag after executable latency
- [statement] Finance Data Cloud recommends using ts_capture for information available to a strategy at decision time; building features on ts_exchange assumes zero feed latency. This is vendor methodology, not independent validation of SOL trading profitability. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-18) — https://www.financedatacloud.com/research/capture-vs-exchange-timestamps · keywords: SOL cross-venue lead-lag after executable latency
- [statement] In their Bitcoin-market study, Albers and coauthors associate a large taker fee and maker rebate with lagging behavior. Treat this as a historical Bitcoin finding; SOL applicability requires separate measurement. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.09750 · keywords: SOL cross-venue lead-lag after executable latency
- [statement] Albers and coauthors explicitly omit market impact and latency concerns from the discussed historical taker PnL calculation. That calculation is not direct evidence of performance after executable latency, and its Bitcoin setting does not establish a SOL effect. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.09750 · keywords: SOL cross-venue lead-lag after executable latency
- [statement] The Cross-Exchange-Arbitrage-Engine README leaves its results section as a template awaiting real data output. Its description is a research design, not empirical evidence that a latency-adjusted SOL edge survives. (low confidence) — https://github.com/YHQZ1/Cross-Exchange-Arbitrage-Engine · keywords: SOL cross-venue lead-lag after executable latency
- [statement] Divyasshree N’s working-paper description reports SOL DEX leadership over Binance with a 40-minute lead, using 1-minute OHLC observations from September 4-5, 2025. Treat this as an attributed coarse-bar observation; that description does not establish a latency-adjusted executable SOL perpetual strategy. (low confidence) — https://zenodo.org/records/17085264 · keywords: SOL cross-venue lead-lag after executable latency
- [statement] In Albers and colleagues’ historical Bitcoin study, the simple pairwise taker strategies all had negative PnL after default execution fees. This historical BTC result is counterevidence to treating statistical venue predictability alone as a profitable SOL trade. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.09750 · keywords: SOL cross-venue lead-lag after executable latency
